chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Shazan ibn al-Khalil who said, 'And I wrote from his book with a chain for him raising it to Isa ibn Abdullah,' he said, 'Isa ibn Abdullah said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):'

'May I be sacrificed for you, what is worship?' He said: 'The good intention in obedience, from the aspects from which Allah is obeyed. Indeed, O Isa, you will not be a believer until you know the abrogating from the abrogated.'

He said, 'I said, may I be sacrificed for you, and what is the knowledge of the abrogating from the abrogated?' So he said: 'Is it not that you are with the Imam, settling your self upon the good intention in his obedience, so that Imam passes away and another Imam comes, so you settle your self upon the good intention in his obedience?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'This is the knowledge of the abrogating from the abrogated.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of worship and the meaning of knowing the abrogating and abrogated verses according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates 'good intention' (husn al-niyyah) as the essence of worship, linking it directly to the epistemological necessity of distinguishing between abrogating (naskh) and abrogated (mansukh) divine rulings. He contextualizes this knowledge within the framework of Imamate, illustrating that just as one Imam succeeds another with potentially new legal directives, the believer’s steadfast intention in obedience remains the constant anchor of faith. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that understanding the dynamic nature of revelation through the Imam is integral to true monotheistic practice.
